strait-of-hormuz.name: Strait of Hormuz
strait-of-hormuz.summary: Waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, bordered by Iran and Oman, and the only sea passage out of the Persian Gulf.

bab-al-mandab-strait.name: Bab al-Mandab Strait
bab-al-mandab-strait.summary: A strategic strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean.

hejaz.name: Hejaz
hejaz.summary: A historical region of western Arabia, in modern Saudi Arabia, containing the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, the first and second holiest sites in Islam.

al-ula.name: Al-Ula
al-ula.summary: An ancient oasis city in northwest Arabia on the incense trade route, once capital of the Lihyanites and near the Nabataean site of Hegra.

south-arabia.name: South Arabia
south-arabia.summary: Historical region covering the southern Arabian Peninsula, mainly present-day Yemen but once including parts of Saudi Arabia and Oman, inhabited largely by Arabic-speaking Arab tribes.

umm-al-nar-culture.name: Umm al-Nar culture
umm-al-nar-culture.summary: Early Bronze Age culture that existed around 2600 to 2000 BCE in what is now the UAE and northern Oman, acting as a trading link between Sumer in Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley.

tihamah.name: Tihamah
tihamah.summary: The Red Sea coastal plain of the Arabian Peninsula, running from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Bab el Mandeb strait.

wadi-suq-culture.name: Wadi Suq culture
wadi-suq-culture.summary: The culture that defined human settlement in the United Arab Emirates and Oman from about 2000 to 1300 BCE, following the Umm Al Nar culture and named after a seasonal watercourse in Oman.

sargon-of-akkad.name: Sargon of Akkad
sargon-of-akkad.summary: First ruler of the Akkadian Empire, who conquered Sumeria's city-states in the 24th to 23rd centuries BC and is sometimes seen as history's first emperor; he later became a legendary figure in Assyrian literature.

naram-sin-of-akkad.name: Naram-Sin
naram-sin-of-akkad.summary: A ruler of Akkad who reigned around 2255–2218 BC, grandson of Sargon, under whom the empire reached its greatest extent and who was the first Mesopotamian king to claim divinity.

magan-civilization.name: Magan
magan-civilization.summary: Ancient region in modern-day Oman and the UAE, referenced in Sumerian texts from around 2300 BCE as a source of copper and diorite for Mesopotamia.

dilmun.name: Dilmun
dilmun.summary: Ancient civilization in eastern Arabia covering modern Bahrain, Kuwait and eastern Saudi Arabia, a major Bronze Age trading centre between Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley described in Sumerian myth as a paradise.

middle-assyrian-empire.name: Middle Assyrian Empire
middle-assyrian-empire.summary: Assyria's first period as an empire, from about 1363 BC to 912 BC, during which it became the dominant power of northern Mesopotamia.

archaeological-sites-of-bat-al-khutm-and.name: Al-Khutm
archaeological-sites-of-bat-al-khutm-and.summary: Part of a group of Bronze Age beehive tombs from the Hafit period (3rd millennium BC) near a palm grove in Oman, declared a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1988.
archaeological-sites-of-bat-al-khutm-and.source_title: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn

ancient-south-arabian-script.name: Ancient South Arabian script
ancient-south-arabian-script.summary: An abjad writing system used in South Arabia from the late 2nd millennium BCE to the 6th century CE, ancestor of the Ge'ez script and sibling of the Phoenician alphabet.

hadhramaut.name: Hadhramaut
hadhramaut.summary: A region in the southern Arabian Peninsula, traditionally explained as meaning 'court of death,' stretching from the Empty Quarter desert to the Arabian Sea coast.

proto-sinaitic-script.name: Proto-Sinaitic script
proto-sinaitic-script.summary: A Middle Bronze Age writing system known from about 30 to 40 inscriptions in the Sinai Peninsula, an early ancestor of alphabetic writing behind the Phoenician, Greek, and Latin alphabets.

abjad.name: Abjad
abjad.summary: Writing system in which only consonants are represented by letters, leaving vowels to be inferred by the reader; the term was coined by linguist Peter T. Daniels in 1990.

ur-nanshe.name: Ur-Nanshe
ur-nanshe.summary: First king of the First Dynasty of Lagash, around 2520 BC, known for building canals and temples and for defending Lagash against the rival city of Umma.

lagash.name: Lagash
lagash.summary: An ancient Sumerian city-state near the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in what is now Iraq, one of the oldest cities of the ancient Near East.

meluhha.name: Meluhha
meluhha.summary: The Sumerian name for a major Bronze Age trading partner of Sumer, generally identified by scholars with the Indus Valley Civilisation.

ur-nammu.name: Ur-Nammu
ur-nammu.summary: Sumerian king who founded the Third Dynasty of Ur around 2100 BC; best remembered for the Code of Ur-Nammu, the oldest surviving legal code, and for starting the Ziggurat of Ur.

burna-buriash-ii.name: Burna-Buriash II
burna-buriash-ii.summary: Kassite king who ruled Babylon (Karduniaš) around 1359 to 1333 BC, during the Late Bronze Age.

il-ippa-ra.name: Ilī-ippašra
il-ippa-ra.summary: A Babylonian who may have been adopted or apprenticed under Kassite king Kurigalzu I and rose to become an official, possibly governor of Dilmun, under Burna-Buriaš II, around 1359–1333 BC.

nippur.name: Nippur
nippur.summary: An ancient Sumerian city in what is now Iraq, the special seat of worship of the god Enlil, occupied from the Ubaid period onward.

qal-at-al-bahrain.name: Qal'at al-Bahrain
qal-at-al-bahrain.summary: An archaeological site and fort in Bahrain occupied from around 2300 BC to the 18th century, once the capital of the Dilmun civilization and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

first-sealand-dynasty.name: Sealand dynasty
first-sealand-dynasty.summary: A dynasty of southern Mesopotamian kings, roughly 1732 to 1475 BCE, that broke free of the Old Babylonian Empire and ruled a swampy southern region called Sealand.

kassites.name: Kassites
kassites.summary: A people from the Zagros Mountains who controlled Babylonia under the Kassite dynasty from about 1531 to 1155 BC, ruling first from Babylon and later from Dur-Kurigalzu.

ras-al-jinz.name: Ras al-Jinz
ras-al-jinz.summary: The easternmost point of the Arabian Peninsula, in Oman, a turtle nesting site where archaeological finds show ancient links to the Indus Valley.

indus-valley-civilisation.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
indus-valley-civilisation.summary: A Bronze Age civilisation of South Asia lasting from about 3300 to 1300 BCE, one of four great centres of the ancient world alongside Egypt, Mesopotamia and China, known through sites like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

al-natah.name: al-Natah
al-natah.summary: A Bronze Age archaeological site in Saudi Arabia's Khaybar Oasis, a walled town of about 1.5 hectares occupied from around 2400 to 1500 BCE.

khaybar.name: Khaybar
khaybar.summary: An oasis north of Medina in Saudi Arabia, inhabited by Jews before Muslims under Muhammad conquered it at the Battle of Khaybar in 628 CE.

menhir.name: Menhir
menhir.summary: A large upright stone placed by humans, typically from the Bronze Age, found across Europe, Africa and Asia and thought to have served ritual or territorial purposes.

isin-larsa-period.name: Isin-Larsa period
isin-larsa-period.summary: A phase of Mesopotamian history, roughly 2025–1763 BCE, between the fall of the Third Dynasty of Ur and Hammurabi's conquest, marked by the rival kingdoms of Isin and Larsa.

akkadian-language.name: Akkadian language
akkadian-language.summary: The earliest documented Semitic language, spoken in ancient Mesopotamia from the mid-third millennium BC until gradually replaced by Aramaic by the 8th century BC, written in cuneiform script.

akkadian-empire.name: Akkadian Empire
akkadian-empire.summary: An ancient kingdom established around 2300 BCE, often considered the first empire in world history, uniting Akkadian and Sumerian speakers across Mesopotamia under Sargon of Akkad and his successors.

early-dynastic-period-mesopotamia.name: Early Dynastic Period (Mesopotamia)
early-dynastic-period-mesopotamia.summary: An era in Mesopotamia, roughly 2900 to 2350 BC, marked by competing city-states before Sargon united the region as the Akkadian Empire.

sumer.name: Sumer
sumer.summary: The earliest known civilization, in southern Mesopotamia (now south-central Iraq), emerging between the 5th and 4th millennium BCE; its cities produced the world's earliest known written texts.

hafit-period.name: Hafit period
hafit-period.summary: An early Bronze Age culture in the United Arab Emirates and Oman from about 3200 to 2600 BCE, named after distinctive beehive burial tombs found near Al Ain.

shimal.name: Shimal
shimal.summary: A settlement in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, linked to the Shihuh tribe and the founding of the port of Julfar, with an archaeological site dating back to 2600–2000 BC.

ras-al-khaimah.name: Ras Al Khaimah
ras-al-khaimah.summary: Port city and capital of the emirate of the same name in the UAE, successor to the historic Islamic-era trading hub of Julfar.

hajar-mountains.name: Hajar Mountains
hajar-mountains.summary: One of the highest mountain ranges on the Arabian Peninsula, shared by northern Oman and the eastern UAE, separating Oman's coastal plain from its desert plateau.

fujairah.name: Fujairah
fujairah.summary: Capital city of the Emirate of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, on the Gulf of Oman at the foothills of the Hajar Mountains.

karen-frifelt.name: Karen Frifelt
karen-frifelt.summary: Danish archaeologist and librarian (1925-2012), a pioneer of Arabian Gulf archaeology who helped define early cultures of the United Arab Emirates and Oman, including leading the first expedition into Oman in 1972.

jemdet-nasr-period.name: Jemdet Nasr period
jemdet-nasr-period.summary: An archaeological culture of southern Mesopotamia dated to about 3100–2900 BC, developing out of the earlier Uruk period and named after the site where it was first identified.

sohar.name: Sohar
sohar.summary: The capital of Oman's Al Batinah North Governorate, an ancient port on the Gulf of Oman and, by legend, the birthplace of Sinbad the Sailor.

jebel-buhais.name: Jebel Buhais
jebel-buhais.summary: A rocky outcrop and archaeological site in Sharjah, UAE, containing an extensive necropolis with burials dating back to the 5th millennium BCE, the oldest radiometrically dated inland burial site in the UAE.
